46488	[FFB300]Guild Level[-]\n1. Guild level is related to the overall activity of the guild members. Guild level calculations are done every Monday at 4:00 AM. If the activity requirement corresponding to the level is reached at the time of settlement, the guild level will increase.\n2. Every week, the guild needs to consume a certain amount of activity points to maintain the guild level. If the guild's activity is less than the level requirement after the settlement, the guild will be downgraded and the corresponding level rewards will be withdrawn.\n3. The activity points required to maintain different levels are different:\nLevel 1: {0}, Level 2: {1}, Level 3: {2}, Level 4: {3}, Level 5: {4}, Level 6: {5}, Level 7: {6}\n4. Guild size is limited to 20 people at first. This limit can be increased by leveling up the guild or purchasing a guild expansion.\n5. Raising the guild level can also unlock more items in the exchange store, more activity rewards, and more guild icons and icon frames.\n\n[FFB300]Guild Management[-]\n1. Each guild can have 1 Guild Leader, 3 Elders, and 1 Acting Leader.\n2. A Guild Leader can: appoint or demote Elders, approve join requests, kick out members, change the slogan and announcement, change the guild name, expand the guild, and change the guild location. An Elder can: approve join requests, kick out members, change the slogan and announcement, and expand the guild.\n3. All guild members can invite their friends and other players to join the guild. The administrators can send out a maximum of 30 guild invitations per day, and ordinary members can send out a maximum of 10 invitations per day. Players can invite their guildmates using the team-up function.\n4. Members may not leave or be kicked out of the guild within {7} minutes of joining.\n5. When a Guild Leader has been offline for longer than 30 days, to keep the Guild running, members who are in this guild for longer than 7 days may apply to become the Acting Leader. Position is effective upon application. If an Acting Leader is offline for longer than 7 days, their position is automatically invalidated. An Acting Leader has the same authority as the Guild Leader, except for the ability to disband the guild.
46489	[FFB300]Activity[-]\n1. Accumulating Guild Activity Points can level up the guild. Leveling up the guild unlocks more guild privileges, more activity rewards, and more items in the exchange store.\n2. Guild privileges include: additional gold and experience, daily gold limit increased and guild member limit increased.\n3. Ways to earn Activity Points:\na. Daily missions: Each daily mission completion provides {0} Activity Points.\nb. Team up and play matches with guildmates: Teaming up with guild members to participate in any game mode will earn you Activity Points. The longer you play, the more Activity Points you earn.\nc. Guild Wars: Participating in the Guild Wars will earn you a large amount of Activity Points. The longer you participate, the more Activity Points you earn.\n d. Spend diamonds: you will also earn Activity Points when you use diamonds to purchase items (with a weekly limit).\n4. After a player leaves the guild, their My Activity Points will be reset to zero. However, the settled Guild Activity Points will not decrease.
46490	BR Guild Wars\n1. Each Guild Wars season consists of several rounds, with each round opening the Guild Wars mode once. Multiple phases may be included in a round. While you can participate during each phase, the phases all belong to the same round. The round scores earned in the same season will accumulate, and all scores will be reset at the beginning of the next season.\n2. Players must team up with guild members to start matchmaking. Participating in matches will yield participation rewards.\n3. Players can play matches during the match time. At the end of the Guild Wars round, the scores from the player's best {0} matches will be taken, and the sum of the {1} match scores will be the player's total score for this round.\n4. Score calculation: Rank Score + Elimination Score.\na. Rank Score: When a player comes in 1st place in a match, they receive a Rank Score of 12; 2nd place receives a Rank Score of 9; 3rd place receives a Rank Score of 8; 4th place receives a Rank Score of 7; 5th place receives a Rank Score of 6; 6th place receives a Rank Score of 5; 7th place receives a Rank Score of 4; 8th place receives a Rank Score of 3; 9th place receives a Rank Score of 2; 10th place receives a Rank Score of 1; and 11th place and subsequent rankings do not receive any Rank Score.\nb. Elimination Score: Every enemy eliminated in a match is worth 4 points.\n5. After each round, "Guild Honor Titles" will be awarded to the guilds on the leaderboard.\n6. If a player quits their guild or gets banned, the Guild Wars Score they earned will be deducted.\n\nCS Guild Wars\n1. Each Guild Wars season consists of several rounds, with each round opening the Guild Wars mode once. Multiple phases may be included in a round. While you can participate during each phase, the phases all belong to the same round. The round scores earned in the same season will accumulate, and all scores will be reset at the beginning of the next season.\n2. Players must team up with guild members to start matchmaking. Participating in matches will yield participation rewards.\n3. Players can play matches during the match time, with a limit of 7 matches per round. Each victory gives a score of 100; each winning round your team lead gives a score of 1; you will not receive any score if you lose a match.\n4. After each round, "Guild Honor Titles" will be awarded to the guilds on the leaderboard.\n5. Only teams with the same number of victories will be matched together.\n6. If a player quits their guild or gets banned, the Guild Wars Score they earned will be deducted.
46491	[FFB300]Guild News[-]\n1. When guild members meet specific conditions, a message will automatically be triggered and sent to the Guild News channel.\n2. All members can respond to guild news with emoticons.\n\n[FFB300]Star Member[-]\n1. The Guild News channel has a Star Members display board, showcasing outstanding guild members.\n2. Criteria include: Highest BR Winning Streak, Highest CS Winning Streak, Highest BR Rank, and Highest CS Rank.\n3. If multiple players have the same number of winning streak or rank, only the player who meets the conditions first will be displayed.\n\n[FFB300]Guild Announcement[-]\n1. Administrators can edit the announcement on the Guild News page and the Set Guild Info. page. New announcements will be highlighted on the guild overview page.
46492	[FFB300]Member List[-]\nPlayers can view guild member information from the member list. After use, it can increase the priority of the guild on the Guild Recommendation page. Each promotion lasts for 24 hours. The first promotion of each week will consume Gold, and the subsequent promotions will consume Diamonds.

64889	Scene View
64890	The performance editor has two views: Scene View and Track View. In Scene View:\n1. Directly select a scene object to create a track for it, or tap the Create Track button to do so.\n2. When a keyframe is selected or when the Record button is enabled, use scene editing tools to edit.\n3. In this view, you can precise edit a track and preview the effects quickly.
64891	Track View
64892	The performance editor has two views: Scene View and Track View. In Track View:\n1. Tap the Create track button to create a track.\n2. When a keyframe is selected or the record button is enabled, open the content panel to edit.\n3. In the view, you can see more tracks at once, making it easier to align content on the tracks.
64893	Create Track
64894	In the performance editor, you can manage actors, play sound effects, and more through individual tracks. Each track functions like a crew member in a production team. Currently, the performance editor provides the following tracks:\n1. Actor Track: Almost all scene objects can serve as actors. You can use this track to control an object's movement from one point to another, as well as its rotation and scaling. Additionally, you can use this camera for cinematic movements and preview effects in real time.\n2. Audio Track: Select this track and add audio clips to play specified sound effects at specific times.\n3. NPC Track: In addition to controlling movement, rotation and scaling like objects, you can also create animation subtracks that allow NPCs to play various animations continuously.\n4. Event Track: If you want a specific block script to run at a specific event, this track helps you send custom events at keyframe times.\n5. Switch Camera Track: Just like different camera angles in movies, this track help you achieve that if you choose different cameras when creating the clip.\nIn addition to the above tracks, we also support subtracks such as Along Path Track, Animation Track, and more!
64895	Toolbox
64896	When you select a track, you will see a toolbox with tools you can use, such as deleting the track, adding a subtrack, adding a keyframe, or adding a key clip.\nWhen you select a keyframe or key clip, you can use tools like deleting the keyframe or opening up the content panel.\nNote that the position, rotation and scaling tools can only be used when the recording is enabled or when a keyframe is selected.
64897	Console
64898	In the console, you can (in order from left to right on the buttons): \n1. Switch the selected track\n2. Player view: When player view is enabled, you can fully preview the screen that the players see during gameplay.\n3. Record button: IF enabled, you can edit the actor's position, rotation, and scale at any time, and these properties will be automatically recorded as keyframes.\n4. Play and jump: Similar to a video player, you can pause at any time, move forward 1 sec, move back 1 sec\nIn addition to the above functions, you can also:\n1. Drag the track to change the time.\n2. Press and hold the keyframe or key clips to move them.\n3. More features are waiting for you to explore!
64899	Play performance
64900	You can play the performance you created by one of the two ways:\n1. Find Performance Trigger in the object bar and edit the object property so that any player entering the trigger will play the corresponding performance.\n2. Use a block script to create a performance.

67050	1. New gameplay mode: Party Parkour. In this mode, players control mini characters and experience a brand-new parkour adventure. This mode is still in testing (some APIs do not work in this mode. Please refer to the tutorial for details).\n2. The classic Bermuda map is now available in Craftland. Iconic areas such as Old Peak and Rim Nam Village have returned, waiting for you to explore!\n\n3. Added a New Year theme to AI generation, and a new racing theme: downhill track to parkour templates.
67051	1. Added a new map gameplay type option. When publishing, you can select a gameplay type for the map to help the system recommend the map more accurately to players who may enjoy that gameplay.\n2. When publishing or updating a map, a new information completeness prompt pop-up has been added. Only maps with complete information will receive exposure and push notifications on the homepage.\n3. The map code now features a short code function. Newly published or updated maps will automatically be assigned a short code, making sharing easier. The original long map code can still be used.
67052	1. Selected objects in the scene will remain synchronized with the Object Manager.\n2. Object Manager optimization: now supports hiding, locating, and multi-selecting objects within the Object Manager.\n3. Multi-selection of objects now supports box selection, making batch editing more efficient.
67053	1. Asset Store now supports textures, sound effects, and more. Plenty of texture and music resources will be available. Creators can use them, along with basic geometrical shapes, sound effect entities, block logic, and more, to enrich their maps!\n 2. In future versions, a custom upload feature will be available, allowing creators to upload their own resources and have more freedom in map creation.
67054	1. Added a permanent photo button, allowing players to take and share photos in Craftland. Shared images include map information and can be saved locally or viewed in the in-game album.\n2. Added new block templates.\n3. Text widgets in the UI editor now support bold, italic, and underline font styles.\n4. Zombies' limbs can now be torn off by dealing DMG to them for a more realistic effect.\n5. Optimized component display logic: components that cannot take effect temporarily are now hidden, making the editor interface cleaner and more user-friendly.\n\nDiscover more new content and stay tuned for more powerful features in the future!

69008	Feature Overview\n1. The Nearby Player Recommendation is an optional feature to enrich your gaming experience.\n2. Your location information will only be obtained and used with your explicit authorization, and it will be used to recommend nearby players to you.\n3. Declining authorization will not affect your other in-game experiences; only this feature will be unavailable.\n\nInformation Collection and Use\n1. After granting authorization, location information is only collected while you are using this feature.\n2. After you are offline, location data is automatically deleted.\n3. Your precise location information will not be displayed to other players; only an approximate distance range will be shown.\n4. You can also adjust the settings to disable the display of the approximate range or opt out of being recommended to nearby players.\n5. For the safety of your account and the game's social environment, we will also run anti-cheat detection on location info to prevent malicious players from using cheats to alter their location.\n\nAuthorization and Cancellation\n1. When using the feature for the first time, a mobile system authorization pop-up will appear. You may choose to grant or decline the authorization.\n2. You may turn off the location permission for this game anytime through your mobile device's settings.\n3. Once it's turned off, we will not collect your location information.

78294	BR-RANKED
78295	There are 6 divisions (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Heroic) in Ranked, each with some sub-divisions for you to progress. In Battle Royale, achievements such as getting high placing in matches, eliminating enemies, helping up teammates, dealing damage will all increase the RP you get from each match. In Clash Squad, progression is only awarded to match winners.
78296	When your RP reaches a certain level, you will be promoted to the next division. Likewise, if your RP drops to a certain level, you will be demoted to a lower division.
78297	As you progress along each division, you will receive rewards (one-time only). When the season ends, season rewards will be given according to the highest division you achieved in the entire season.
78298	Ranked leaderboards are sorted by division and sub-divisions. You can see how you place amongst your friends. If your rank is high enough, you may even find yourself in the global leaderboards.
78299	At the end of each season, rank will be reset. Depending on your performance in the previous season, you might begin at a higher rank when the new season begins.
